## Objective

Deliver the provider-neutral direct bootstrap, full project-local path confinement, consumer resources, immutable wheel workflow, and focused verification.

## Scope

- Memory Service source, interfaces, configuration, package resources, documentation, and tests

## Entry conditions

- PHASE-001 is completed with a current protected-state baseline.

## Exit criteria

- TASK-002 through TASK-006 have current evidence and direct bootstrap creates no preview or user-wide state.

## Risks

- A direct initialization route could weaken existing safety if it removes preflight rather than only preview UX.
- Provider import order can create user-wide state before configuration.

## TASK-002 - Add the direct Memory System bootstrap contract

Add one provider-neutral direct bootstrap operation used by Python and command-line entry points that performs required internal validation and initialization in one authorized invocation without producing or accepting a preview artifact or preview digest.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-010, REQ-017, REQ-018 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | Projects/Sys4AI-Memory-Service/src/sys4ai_memory/initialization/, Projects/Sys4AI-Memory-Service/src/sys4ai_memory/interfaces/models.py, Projects/Sys4AI-Memory-Service/src/sys4ai_memory/interfaces/python.py, Projects/Sys4AI-Memory-Service/src/sys4ai_memory/cli.py, Projects/Sys4AI-Memory-Service/src/sys4ai_memory/service/dispatcher.py |
| Dependencies | TASK-001 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-05T01:02:09.591564Z |

### Risks

- Removing the existing preview path globally could weaken unrelated destructive-operation controls.
- A partial bootstrap could leave derived state without a valid receipt.

### Acceptance criteria

- A direct init-memory request performs configuration, identity, source-discovery dry run, secret, and path checks before any write.
- The bootstrap neither generates nor consumes a preview object or preview digest.
- Existing preview-and-apply behavior remains available only where still required outside the new-project bootstrap contract, or is explicitly migrated with preserved safety.
- The installed console command constructs a real project-scoped service from validated local configuration without a caller-injected dispatcher, and subsequent installed commands can use initialized state.
- Shared validation and initialization internals serve direct new/manual bootstrap and the separately authorized digest-bound root adoption; preview objects are confined to the root/legacy entry path.

### Planned verification

- Run focused initialization service, dispatcher, Python-interface, and CLI tests.
- Inspect failure injection at every pre-write and publish boundary.
- Search bootstrap output and receipts for preview fields or digest prompts.
- Run the wheel-installed executable in an isolated subprocess with no injected dispatcher; observe initialization then a bounded subsequent exact operation.

## TASK-003 - Confine every provider and model path before import

Preserve existing pre-import data/system/cache/log isolation and close configurable model-cache and runtime identity gaps so all provider, exact-index, audit, receipt, export and model paths resolve beneath the selected project derived boundary.

| Dependencies | TASK-001 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-05T00:53:41.504803Z |

### Risks

- Cognee import creates ~/.cognee/logs when COGNEE_LOGS_DIR is not set first.
- Process-global provider state could leak across projects.

### Acceptance criteria

- The adapter sets project-local DATA_ROOT_DIRECTORY, SYSTEM_ROOT_DIRECTORY, CACHE_ROOT_DIRECTORY, COGNEE_LOGS_DIR, and model-cache paths before import.
- Direct or pre-imported Cognee use fails closed at the adapter boundary.
- Two project configurations produce distinct provider and model paths with no user-wide fallback.
- FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH and every configured model cache use the validated project-local derived boundary rather than hard-coded project_root/models/fastembed.

### Planned verification

- Run provider-boundary and configuration tests in isolated subprocesses.
- Snapshot the user-wide Cognee log directory before and after safe adapter tests and require no new entry.
- Verify all resolved paths remain within the project root and are ignored.

## TASK-004 - Package reusable consumer bootstrap resources

Add versioned provider-neutral configuration, registry, control-record, and receipt templates plus one bootstrap service inside the Memory Service package so every entry route reuses the same executable procedure.

| Dependencies | TASK-002, TASK-003 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-05T01:26:04.550799Z |

### Risks

- Package resources could drift from the runtime schemas or expose a product-specific identity.
- Canonical consumer configuration must remain editable project-owned data after installation.

### Acceptance criteria

- A built wheel contains every bootstrap resource needed to create project-local configuration and control records.
- Resources contain no real project identity, credential, user-home path, or initialized state.
- The bootstrap writes specialized canonical files to the consumer project and does not read editable sibling source.
- Consumer resources include the complete schema, profile config, write policy and optional migration reference closure required by load_registry_bundle, with consumer-safe ownership and no product-specific permission grants.
- A clean consumer loads its registries, configuration and service solely from installed package resources and project-local canonical files.

### Planned verification

- Inspect wheel contents without installation.
- Validate generated consumer files against current schemas and configuration loader.
- Compare all entry routes to the single bootstrap service.
- Load every generated registry reference in a consumer fixture with the product checkout unavailable.

## TASK-005 - Define immutable local wheel production and recording

Add the reproducible local build and artifact-verification workflow that records Memory Service version and SHA-256 and supports non-editable installation into a consumer environment.

| Dependencies | TASK-002, TASK-003 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-05T01:26:11.360022Z |

### Risks

- An unlocked build or stale wheel could make source and installed behavior diverge.
- A wheel path or build log could be mistaken for publication.

### Acceptance criteria

- The workflow builds from the locked checkout, emits one versioned wheel, computes its SHA-256, and produces a non-secret local receipt.
- A clean consumer environment installs the exact wheel without editable or sibling-path metadata.
- No package is uploaded or published.
- The build workflow records Python, backend version, locked runtime dependencies and artifact hash; any missing build tooling resolution is explicitly authorized before installation.

### Planned verification

- Build the wheel twice from unchanged source and compare version, contents, and digest policy.
- Inspect installed metadata and import origin in an isolated consumer environment.
- Mutate only a disposable build-source fixture after installation and prove installed runtime bytes remain unchanged; preserve the live product checkout.
